title: Vocal Jazz: battery-in check of the wireless mics at FOH
about: Gameplay slice v2 (PRODUCT_DESIGN.md sections 45, 46, 94 and principle 4.10): the battery-in check at FOH. One signal chain (handheld -> receiver -> X32 input), one fault (a handheld powered on but muted), one objective that completes only on verified evidence, one hint ladder, a visible step list, 'Check the rest' after three mics by hand, and one debrief. Everything marked tentative or unknown below is a placeholder to field-calibrate, not room truth.

clock.status: tentative: 4:50 doors / 5:00 rehearsal come from PRODUCT_DESIGN section 40. Per-action and per-move seconds are placeholders (section 89: field-calibrate); owner, 2026-09-27: make each check faster for now (was 5 s / 4 s), timing to be adjusted later.

setup.status: owner, 2026-09-27: about 13 musicians, so 13 mics + 2 spares (in case one dies from bad batteries or frequencies) + 1 at FOH for the A1 to talk to the stage through the monitors = 16, on channels 1-16.
setup.note: X32 and receivers start powered on, and every handheld starts on with good batteries, so the transmitter mute is the only fault (one fault per section 94).

roles.value: This slice is the battery-in check at FOH (A2 alone, next to the receivers and the X32), as soon as batteries go into each mic and before the mics go to the stage. The official line check is later, on stage: musicians make sound, the A1 confirms each channel at the X32.

mic_roles.status: owner, 2026-09-27: channels 1-13 are the musicians' mics. 14, 15 and 16 are three interchangeable spares kept at FOH: any of them can be the A1's talkback mic, or the emergency mic the A2 runs down to the stage to replace a dead one. Roles don't change the check yet.

start_state.value: every handheld is already on, with batteries in; putting the batteries in is not simulated yet
start_state.status: simplification for v2 (owner, 2026-09-27): battery insertion arrives with the battery faults

ptu6000-rx.label: Phenyx Pro PTU-6000 receivers
ptu6000-rx.unknown: whether a muted transmitter still shows RF on the receiver. Only audio present / absent is modelled.
ptu6000-rx.units_status: current fact (owner, 2026-09-27): each receiver unit is 8 channels, top unit = 1-8, next = 9-16, and so on

devices_status: Owner, 2026-09-27: mics are named by windscreen colour then ring colour, and that is how people mostly refer to them (black red = 1, black orange = 2, black black = 7, black grey = 8, grey red = 9, grey orange = 10, grey black = 15, grey grey = 16). Ring order (owner-confirmed): red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, black, grey. Mics 17-24: treat as no windscreen for now (owner, 2026-09-27; may change). Handhelds live in the FOH mic drawer (manifest row IMG_4127). State `battery`: "ok" is the only value used in v2; see future_faults. RF group/channel (owner, 2026-09-27): mic N is NOT RF channel N. Each mic has its own group and channel number, which selects a frequency and is set by pairing with its receiver (a procedure of its own). Values not recorded yet (null = unknown). For now every mic is assumed paired; an unpaired mic, or any other problem, is simply a 'bad mic' that gets swapped for a spare. Pairing can be a later level.

fault.label: A wireless handheld is powered on but muted
fault.target: one handheld, chosen by the seed from placement.channels

placement.status: owner, 2026-09-27: the muted mic should be the 2nd or 3rd of the first 3 checked by hand (the drawer and the step list go in colour order, i.e. channel order)

fault.note: owner, 2026-09-27: on-but-muted is really an on-stage line-check fault (a freshly powered mic starts unmuted, since a power cycle clears the mute). It stays here for v2 and moves when the line check is built.

objective.label: Battery-in check: the wireless mics
objective.goal: Before the mics go to the stage, verify every one: talking into it shows signal at its X32 input.
objective.source: PRODUCT_DESIGN sections 45 (battery-in check; speak into each mic), 55 (goals, not recipes; complete only after verification)

steps.text: Take the right mic from the drawer: windscreen colour, then ring colour.
Put two batteries in from the charger, the right way round.
At the X32, talk into it: its channel's meter must move.
Put it on the chair left of FOH.

procedure.optional: Reading the mic's display (group/channel, battery, mute) isn't needed when everything works; it's how you troubleshoot one that doesn't.
procedure.status: owner, 2026-09-27: this is the procedure (grab the right mic by colour, batteries in from the charger, switch it on, check the meter at the X32 = the win criterion). Battery insertion arrives with the battery work.

skip.label: Check the rest
skip.does: for the remaining mics in channel order, the same routine as by hand, carrying up to two at a time (take them, then at the X32 for each: talk into it, put it on the chair), costing the same game time; it stops at the first mic whose X32 input shows no signal, and leaves it (and any unchecked partner) in your hands at the X32
skip.status: PRODUCT_DESIGN 4.10 (owner, 2026-09-27); 3 by hand is from the brief

hints.text: No signal is reaching the receiver. Where could the problem be upstream?
The transmitter is muted. Unmute it and verify signal.
